title: Scarcity & opportunity cost
examples: Can you give me an example of scarcity in everyday life?
How do governments deal with scarcity?
Is opportunity cost always about money?

explain.say: Today we will learn about scarcity and choice. Scarcity means that wants are greater than available resources. Resources are things we use to satisfy our wants. We cannot have everything we want because resources are limited.

Because of scarcity, we are forced to make choices. A choice is simply selecting one option from several possibilities. Every time we choose one thing, we are giving up other things. This is a basic concept in economics.

draw.text: Scarcity forces us to make choices.

explain.say: When you make a choice, you face trade-offs. A trade-off means giving up something to get something else. Think about time; spending time studying means less time playing games. This is a simple trade-off.

draw.text: Trade-off: Giving up one thing for another.

explain.say: The opportunity cost is the most important part. It is the value of the next best alternative you give up. If you choose apples, your opportunity cost might be the oranges you did not pick. It is what you sacrifice.

draw.text: Opportunity cost = Next best alternative forgone.

explain.say: Imagine you have only enough money for one movie ticket. You must choose between seeing a comedy or an action film.

draw.text: Opportunity cost: next best alternative given up.

faq.q: What if I have enough money for everything I want?
faq.a: If you have unlimited resources, scarcity does not exist for you. However, in the real world, resources like time or land are usually limited.
asks: Does scarcity only apply to money?

faq.q: Is the opportunity cost always something physical?
faq.a: No, the opportunity cost can be non-physical things too. It could be enjoyment, or knowledge gained from the next best option.
asks: What is the cost of time?

faq.q: If I choose option A, is the opportunity cost always option B?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The opportunity cost is only the next best option you gave up. You must rank your choices to find that one.
asks: Do I have to list all my options?
How do I find the best alternative?

faq.q: Does a business always face scarcity?
faq.a: Yes, businesses face scarcity regarding resources like labour, raw materials, and capital. They must make choices about what to produce.
asks: Do businesses ever have unlimited resources?

faq.q: Is opportunity cost the same as the cost price?
faq.a: No, they are different concepts. The cost price is what you pay money for. Opportunity cost is what you give up by making a choice.
asks: Is opportunity cost just the money spent?
What is the difference between cost and opportunity cost?

facts: Scarcity means that human wants exceed the available resources.
Choices must be made because resources are limited.
A trade-off is the act of giving up one thing to gain another.
Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative forgone.

quiz.say: A baker has enough flour for one hundred loaves of bread or fifty cakes. If the baker makes the bread, what is the opportunity cost?

options.show: The total number of items made.
options.say: The total number of items made.

options.show: The fifty cakes the baker could have made.
options.say: The fifty cakes the baker could have made.

options.show: The flour used to make the bread.
options.say: The flour used to make the bread.

options.show: The effort the baker put into the bread.
options.say: The effort the baker put into the bread.

quiz.why: The opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative. Since cakes were the other option, that is the cost.

wrong.0: This option is a summary and does not represent the specific alternative given up.
wrong.2: The flour is a resource, not the cost of the choice.
wrong.3: Effort is a resource, but the cost is measured by the forgone item.

quiz.say: A student has a limited budget. They can buy either a new book or a cinema ticket. If they buy the book, what is the opportunity cost?

options.show: The total money they had saved.
options.say: The total money they had saved.

options.show: The cinema ticket they could have bought.
options.say: The cinema ticket they could have bought.

options.show: The time spent reading the book.
options.say: The time spent reading the book.

quiz.why: The opportunity cost is the next best alternative. If the ticket was the next best thing, that is the cost.

wrong.0: This is the total available resource, not the specific alternative given up.
wrong.2: The price of the book is the monetary cost, not the opportunity cost.
wrong.3: Time spent is a resource, but the cost is defined by the forgone item.
